```{r}
# Loading the passcode dataset
Password_data <- read.csv("DSL-StrongPasswordData.csv", header = TRUE)
head(Password_data)
```
```{r}
# Loading libraries
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(caret)        # Used for data partitioning
```

```{r}
# To View structure
glimpse(Password_data)

# How many unique subjects?
length(unique(Password_data$subject))


```

```{r}
# filtering column called 'rep' (typing repetition index)
filtered_data <- Password_data %>%
  filter(rep >= 31 & rep <= 50)

# to know shape of data
dim(filtered_data)

```

```{r}
set.seed(123)  # for reproducibility

# To Create stratified split
train_index <- createDataPartition(filtered_data$subject, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)

train_data <- filtered_data[train_index, ]
test_data  <- filtered_data[-train_index, ]

# For Viewing class distribution
table(train_data$subject)

```

#Feature Engineering
```{r}
#Creating new three columns total_h_time,total_dd_time,total_ud_time for both train and test sets  
train_data <- train_data %>%
  mutate(
    total_h_time  = rowSums(dplyr::select(., starts_with("H."))),
    total_dd_time = rowSums(dplyr::select(., starts_with("DD."))),
    total_ud_time = rowSums(dplyr::select(., starts_with("UD.")))
  )

test_data <- test_data %>%
  mutate(
    total_h_time  = rowSums(dplyr::select(., starts_with("H."))),
    total_dd_time = rowSums(dplyr::select(., starts_with("DD."))),
    total_ud_time = rowSums(dplyr::select(., starts_with("UD.")))
  )
dim(train_data)
dim(test_data)
```

#Data Preprocessing
```{r}
# Standardizing all numeric columns (except subject) (Its Used for XGBoost and SVM)
library(caret)

preprocess <- preProcess(dplyr::select(train_data, -subject), method = c("center", "scale"))


train_scaled <- predict(preprocess, dplyr::select(train_data, -subject))
test_scaled  <- predict(preprocess, dplyr::select(test_data, -subject))


# Adding subject to column back
train_scaled$subject <- train_data$subject
test_scaled$subject  <- test_data$subject

```

#Baseline Model Building and Evaluation

```{r}
#required libraries to be loaded
library(nnet)
library(MASS)
library(mclust)
library(rpart)
library(randomForest)
library(xgboost)
library(e1071)
library(tibble)

```

```{r}
  #Firstly selecting only three features and applying classification techniques
train_total <- train_data %>% dplyr::select(subject, total_h_time, total_dd_time, total_ud_time)
test_total  <- test_data %>% dplyr::select(subject, total_h_time, total_dd_time, total_ud_time)

# To Make sure that 'subject' is a factor
train_total$subject <- as.factor(train_total$subject)
test_total$subject  <- as.factor(test_total$subject)

```

#Model 1: Multinomial Logistic Regression
```{r}
library(nnet)

log_model <- multinom(subject ~ ., data = train_total)
log_preds <- predict(log_model, newdata = test_total)
log_acc <- mean(log_preds == test_total$subject)

```
2. LDA

```{r}
#Linear Discriminant Analysis
library(MASS)

lda_model <- lda(subject ~ ., data = train_total)
lda_preds <- predict(lda_model, newdata = test_total)$class
lda_acc <- mean(lda_preds == test_total$subject)

```

3. QDA
```{r}
#Quadratic Discriminant Analysis
qda_model <- qda(subject ~ ., data = train_total)
qda_preds <- predict(qda_model, newdata = test_total)$class
qda_acc <- mean(qda_preds == test_total$subject)

```

4. MClustDA
```{r}
#MclustDA discriminant analysis
library(mclust)

mclust_model <- MclustDA(train_total %>% dplyr::select(-subject), train_total$subject)
mclust_preds <- predict(mclust_model, test_total %>% dplyr::select(-subject))$classification
mclust_acc <- mean(mclust_preds == test_total$subject)


```
5. Decision Tree
```{r}
library(rpart)

tree_model <- rpart(subject ~ ., data = train_total, method = "class")
tree_preds <- predict(tree_model, newdata = test_total, type = "class")
tree_acc <- mean(tree_preds == test_total$subject)

```

6. Random Forest
```{r}
library(randomForest)

rf_model <- randomForest(subject ~ ., data = train_total)
rf_preds <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_total)
rf_acc <- mean(rf_preds == test_total$subject)

```

7. XGBoost
```{r}
library(xgboost)

# Preparing data f
x_train <- as.matrix(train_total %>% dplyr::select(total_ud_time, total_dd_time, total_h_time))
x_test  <- as.matrix(test_total  %>% dplyr::select(total_ud_time, total_dd_time, total_h_time))

y_train <- as.numeric(train_total$subject) - 1
y_test  <- as.numeric(test_total$subject) - 1

xgb_model <- xgboost(data = x_train, label = y_train, objective = "multi:softmax",
                     num_class = length(unique(train_total$subject)),
                     nrounds = 30, verbose = 0)

xgb_preds <- predict(xgb_model, x_test)
xgb_acc <- mean(xgb_preds == y_test)

```

8.SVM
```{r}
library(e1071)

svm_model <- svm(subject ~ ., data = train_total, kernel = "radial", cost = 1, gamma = 0.01)
svm_preds <- predict(svm_model, newdata = test_total)
svm_acc <- mean(svm_preds == test_total$subject)

```
Summary Table — Baseline Model Comparison

```{r}

baseline_results <- tibble(
  Model = c("Multinomial Logistic", "LDA", "QDA", "MClustDA",
            "Decision Tree", "Random Forest", "XGBoost", "SVM"),
  Features = "3 total_features",
  Accuracy = c(log_acc, lda_acc, qda_acc, mclust_acc,
               tree_acc, rf_acc, xgb_acc, svm_acc)
)
#To print all baseline models
print(baseline_results)

```
#Now Applying all features on eight models

```{r}
# Performing PCA on training data (excluding subject)
pca_model <- prcomp(train_scaled %>% dplyr::select(-subject), center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Choosing top 17 PCs
n_pcs <- 17

train_pca <- as.data.frame(predict(pca_model, train_scaled %>% dplyr::select(-subject))[, 1:n_pcs])
train_pca$subject <- train_scaled$subject

test_pca <- as.data.frame(predict(pca_model, test_scaled %>% dplyr::select(-subject))[, 1:n_pcs])
test_pca$subject <- test_scaled$subject


```
1.Logistic Regression
```{r}
log_model_pca <- multinom(subject ~ ., data = train_pca)
log_preds_pca <- predict(log_model_pca, newdata = test_pca)
log_acc_pca <- mean(log_preds_pca == test_pca$subject)


```
2.LDA
```{r}
lda_model_pca <- lda(subject ~ ., data = train_pca)
lda_preds_pca <- predict(lda_model_pca, newdata = test_pca)$class
lda_acc_pca <- mean(lda_preds_pca == test_pca$subject)

```
3.QDA
```{r}
qda_model_pca <- qda(subject ~ ., data = train_pca)
qda_preds_pca <- predict(qda_model_pca, newdata = test_pca)$class
qda_acc_pca <- mean(qda_preds_pca == test_pca$subject)

```
4.MclustDA
```{r}
mclust_model_pca <- MclustDA(train_pca %>% dplyr::select(-subject), train_pca$subject)
mclust_preds_pca <- predict(mclust_model_pca, test_pca %>% dplyr::select(-subject))$classification
mclust_acc_pca <- mean(mclust_preds_pca == test_pca$subject)

```

7.XGBoost

```{r}
train_scaled$subject <- as.factor(train_scaled$subject)
test_scaled$subject  <- as.factor(test_scaled$subject)

# To Create a lookup table
subject_levels <- levels(train_scaled$subject)

# here Converting subjects to 0-based numeric labels
y_train_full <- as.integer(train_scaled$subject) - 1
y_test_full  <- as.integer(factor(test_scaled$subject, levels = subject_levels)) - 1

any(is.na(y_train_full))  # checking for nulls
any(is.na(y_test_full))   # so Should be FALSE

```
```{r}
library(xgboost)

x_train_full <- as.matrix(train_scaled %>% dplyr::select(-subject))
x_test_full  <- as.matrix(test_scaled %>% dplyr::select(-subject))

xgb_model_full <- xgboost(data = x_train_full, label = y_train_full, objective = "multi:softmax",
                          num_class = length(subject_levels),
                          nrounds = 30, verbose = 0)

xgb_preds_full <- predict(xgb_model_full, x_test_full)
xgb_acc_full <- mean(xgb_preds_full == y_test_full)

cat("XGBoost Accuracy (Full):", xgb_acc_full, "\n")

```

#Model Tuning
```{r}
```

1.Random Forest
```{r}
# To Control for 5-fold Cross validation
ctrl <- trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5)

# Tuning mtry (number of variables considered at each split)
set.seed(42)
rf_tuned <- train(subject ~ ., data = train_data,
                  method = "rf",
                  trControl = ctrl,
                  tuneGrid = expand.grid(mtry = c(5, 10, 15, 20)))

# printing the Best mtry value
print(rf_tuned$bestTune)
plot(rf_tuned)

# now Predicting on test set
rf_preds_tuned <- predict(rf_tuned, newdata = test_data)
rf_acc_tuned <- mean(rf_preds_tuned == test_data$subject)
cat("Random Forest Tuned Accuracy:", rf_acc_tuned, "\n")


```
2.SVM
```{r}
# Tried with less computational code
# Tuning Grid of C and sigma (gamma)
svm_grid <- expand.grid(
  C = c(1, 5),              # Here fewer cost values
  sigma = c(0.01, 0.1)      # fewer gamma values
)


set.seed(42)
svm_tuned <- train(subject ~ ., data = train_scaled,
                   method = "svmRadial",
                   preProcess = NULL,
                   trControl = ctrl,
                   tuneLength = 3)

svm_preds_tuned <- predict(svm_tuned, newdata = test_scaled)
svm_acc_tuned <- mean(svm_preds_tuned == test_scaled$subject)
cat("SVM Tuned Accuracy (Fast):", svm_acc_tuned, "\n")

```

3.XGBoost
```{r}
# Encoding subject as factor first, then numeric labels
x_train <- as.matrix(train_scaled %>% dplyr::select(-subject))
x_test  <- as.matrix(test_scaled %>% dplyr::select(-subject))
y_train <- train_scaled$subject
y_test  <- test_scaled$subject

# caret compatible data
train_xgb <- train_scaled
train_xgb$subject <- as.factor(train_xgb$subject)

# Tuning the key parameters
xgb_grid <- expand.grid(
  nrounds = 30,
  max_depth = c(4, 6),
  eta = 0.1,
  gamma = 0,
  colsample_bytree = 1,
  min_child_weight = 1,
  subsample = 1
)

set.seed(42)
xgb_tuned <- train(subject ~ ., data = train_xgb,
                   method = "xgbTree",
                   trControl = ctrl,
                   tuneGrid = xgb_grid,
                   verbose = FALSE)
#printing the best parameters
print(xgb_tuned$bestTune)
plot(xgb_tuned)
# now Predicting on test set
xgb_preds_tuned <- predict(xgb_tuned, newdata = test_scaled)
xgb_acc_tuned <- mean(xgb_preds_tuned == test_scaled$subject)
cat("XGBoost Tuned Accuracy (Fast):", xgb_acc_tuned, "\n")

```
#Model Evaluation
```{r}
library(caret)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)
```
```{r}
#Considering the Random Forest is the best model
# Generating confusion matrix
conf_matrix <- confusionMatrix(rf_preds_tuned, test_data$subject)

# Printing full confusion matrix
print(conf_matrix)


```

```{r}
# Extracting class-wise stats
class_stats <- as.data.frame(conf_matrix$byClass)

# Add subject label
class_stats$subject <- rownames(class_stats)

# Keep main metrics
summary_stats <- class_stats %>%
  dplyr::select(subject, Precision = Precision, Recall = Recall, F1 = F1)

# View top/bottom performance classes
summary_stats %>% arrange(F1) %>% head()
summary_stats %>% arrange(desc(F1)) %>% head()

```

```{r}
#Now Creating a dataframe of actual vs. predicted
library(dplyr)

misclass_df <- data.frame(
  actual = test_data$subject,
  predicted = rf_preds_tuned
)

# Keeping only incorrect predictions
misclass_df <- misclass_df %>%
  filter(actual != predicted)

#   To Count confusion pairs
confusion_pairs <- misclass_df %>%
  group_by(actual, predicted) %>%
  summarise(freq = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(freq))

# To View top 10 most confused subject pairs
head(confusion_pairs, 10)


```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

top_confusions <- head(confusion_pairs, 10)

ggplot(top_confusions, aes(x = actual, y = predicted, fill = freq)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = freq), size = 5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "red") +
  labs(title = "Top Confused Subject Pairs",
       x = "Actual Subject", y = "Predicted Subject") +
  theme_minimal()



```

```{r}
confused_pair <- c("s051", "s007")

ggplot(test_data %>% filter(subject %in% confused_pair),
       aes(x = total_h_time, fill = subject)) +
  geom_histogram(alpha = 0.6, bins = 15, position = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Total Hold Time: s051 vs s007") +
  theme_minimal()


```
